newHazards.summary: The refusal the round made operator-facing prints an unrounded float for the remaining room (`latestRoom` is a raw Decimal subtraction).
newHazards.detail: `const latestRoom = Number(latest?.total ?? 0) - Number(latestAgg._sum.amount ?? 0)` (:463) is the only money figure in this string that never passes through `roundMoney` — `amount` does (priceReturn rounds at :541). The message at :470 interpolates it verbatim, and round 3 promoted that string to the resolve toast's description, so with e.g. an invoice total 100.10 already carrying 70.05 of credit the operator reads "exceeds the remaining room 30.049999999999997 on invoice INV-060". Round 4 is what makes this visible-quality matter (the whole point of adding `invoiceNumber` was that the operator acts on this sentence), and the two new pins assert only `toContain("INV-06x")`, so nothing guards the number's shape. Not a correctness defect — the comparison itself uses the 0.001 epsilon and is unaffected — and it does not block landing; the one-line follow-up is `roundMoney(...)` around the subtraction (or formatting both figures at the throw site), ideally with a pin on the rendered digits.

review.reasoning: Both round-4 hazards are genuinely fixed, and I tried to refute each rather than confirm it. Hazard 0's completeness claim holds under a full trace: `billedBasisFor` is private with a single call site, its invoice rows come from exactly one query, that query now selects `invoiceNumber`, and the three sibling `invoices:` selects provably cannot reach the message (they feed the pure `priceReturn`, which composes no string — \"remaining room\" occurs once in the whole service). The pin is no longer self-fulfilling: the `invoicesAsSelected` projector derives fixture rows from the real `select` object on the mock's own args, so a fixture cannot supply a field production never asks for, and the new un-projected negative pin holds the fallback branch from the other side — the two assertions are now about the query and the template separately, which is precisely what the ruling asked for. The executor's extra scope (converting the sibling ret-53f pin to the projector) is a strict improvement, not scope creep: that pin previously asserted `/inv-b/`, i.e. it pinned the raw-UUID shape hazard 0 condemns. Hazard 1 is a pure copy-layer change with the wire contract untouched, `showEstimateReason` fully removed, and no other surface rendering the token. I hunted the two failure modes the brief named and found neither: the added `invoiceNumber` never crosses the wire (processRefund returns `updated`, a separate include-less findUnique at :625, and findAll/findOne strip their invoice graphs), so no DRIVER/CUSTOMER-visible shape changed; and the spec fixture cannot diverge from a second query because the projector reads the args of whichever call it is given and throws loudly if the select is missing — the worst case is a red test, never a false green. The one new finding is cosmetic (an unrounded float in the same refusal string) and is not worth a round of its own: it is a one-line change a follow-up can carry, and forcing another executor pass over `returns.service.ts` costs more risk than it removes. All five regate commands are green (api tsc, api jest 136/136, mobile tsc, mobile jest 30/30, web tsc), prettier is clean on both touched files, `apps/api/src/routes/routes.service.ts` is untouched, and no client identifiers were introduced. Land.
